title: wkayaobama-skills: personal Claude Code skills and commands library
one_liner: Portable library of the owner's Claude Code commands and skills: pipeline salvation plans, Bronze ETL methodology, PDF-to-DOCX salvage scripts and a prompt-level rigor hook.
purpose: A personal, cross-machine knowledge repo for Claude Code. It collects the methods the owner distilled while rescuing the IC'ALPS CRM pipeline (icalps-dashboard: Excel/xlwings + FastAPI bridge + 12-stage PowerShell Bronze ETL called Workflowps) and makes them reusable through one environment variable, CLAUDE__ROOT, that every file uses as its absolute root. It holds two commands (write a salvation plan, execute it checkpoint by checkpoint) and five skills: pipeline-salvation, workflowps (three documents), github-deployment, salvage-pdf-to-word and production-discipline. Only salvage-pdf-to-word ships runnable code (Node + Python scripts that rebuild an untagged PDF into a structured DOCX); production-discipline ships a PowerShell hook that injects a seven-point rigor checklist on decision-like prompts. Everything else is methodology text that is read on demand, never loaded wholesale into a session.
domain: LLM tooling: Claude Code skills, ETL methodology, document salvage
stack: Documented only: PSDuckDB, ImportExcel, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, FastAPI, xlwings

entry_points.what: Asks Claude to write a Pipeline Salvation plan (8 sections) and save it under ~/.claude/plans/ before any code is touched.
Executes a saved plan task by task: sentinel check, run, verify, stop at every checkpoint for confirmation.
Stage 1: walks the pdfjs operator list of page 1 and writes raw.json plus raw.stats.json in top-left coordinates.
Stage 2: renders the first page to PNG and cuts it into N horizontal bands used as visual ground truth.
Stage 3: clusters text items into lines, classifies them with the corpus config, groups blocks and emits output.docx plus output.ir.json.
Stage 4: converts the DOCX to a self-contained HTML preview with mammoth.
The UserPromptSubmit hook command: prints the rigor checklist that Claude Code injects as extra context when the prompt matches the matcher regex.

architecture.responsibility: Declares CLAUDE__ROOT (set once per machine in ~/.bashrc or the PowerShell profile) as the absolute root used by every skill file, maps the tree and says when to invoke each skill. Rule: do not load all skills into every session.

Forces a read-first step, an architecture baseline with a status per stage, then the eight plan sections and the five-level probe ladder. A plan that omits either execution system (Python dashboard or Workflowps) is declared invalid.
Loads and criticises the plan, executes each task with .done sentinel checks, verifies before marking complete, pauses at checkpoints and never declares success before the Success Threshold is met.

Methodology for recovering the working core of a messy pipeline: success threshold, canonical execution boundary, stage contracts, four buckets, runnable spine, probe discipline, guardrail assessment, recovery checkpoints, first action.

Skill named bronze-extraction-pipeline: entity contract, query contract, run-context layout, snapshot capture, state ledger, structural and semantic gates, 12 numbered stages. Maps each concept to files of the PowerShell reference implementation.
Domain-agnostic version of the same pipeline as six principles: entity is the query, content hash as CDC, FK graph propagation, layered gates, run state machine, filesystem as execution graph.

Documents the two optional integrations of the PowerShell pipeline: the Excel approval gate for stage 09 (VBA button or xlwings function writing approved.json) and the FastAPI bridge used by the dashboard and as stage 11 load fallback.

Seven-step recipe that created this repo from icalps-dashboard: create the repo with gh, set CLAUDE__ROOT, copy commands and skills, write the README, push, link back, and reference skills locally instead of remote plugins.

pdfjs-dist walker for page 1: text items via getTextContent, path bounding boxes via getOperatorList with a save/restore/transform matrix stack, y flipped to top-left. Writes raw.json and raw.stats.json.

Corpus-agnostic core: loads config.json, clusters lines, classifies each line, folds lines into blocks (banner, form-question, proc-list, field-slot, paragraph) and emits the DOCX with docx-js plus the IR JSON for audit.
render_canvas.py and slice_canvas.py produce PNG bands to compare against the IR; preview.js turns the DOCX into HTML through mammoth for a fast browser check.

Harness-level rigor gate: a UserPromptSubmit matcher regex runs rigor-reminder.ps1, which prints a seven-point checklist (sequential thinking, read docs, search memory, state assumptions, evidence). Option 2 documents a blocking PreToolUse variant.

data_flow: 1. Library lifecycle: a skill is authored inside a source project (originally icalps-dashboard), copied into commands/ or skills/<name>/ here, committed and pushed; the README tree and the 'When to Use Each Skill' table are updated.

2. On each machine the repo is cloned and CLAUDE__ROOT is exported once; skills are then invoked by asking Claude to read ${CLAUDE__ROOT}/commands/<file>.md, which pulls in the skills it needs by absolute path.

3. Plan flow: write_plan reads both orchestrators, the Workflowps contract and git state, then writes a plan with an architecture baseline and eight sections to ~/.claude/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md.

4. execute_plan reviews the plan, then per task: check the .done sentinel, run the stage or Python step, verify the artifact against its contract, mark completed; it stops at each checkpoint and finally runs probe levels 1 to 4.

5. Reference Bronze pipeline (documented, code lives elsewhere): 00_preflight, 01_extract, 02_repair, 03_delta, 04_cascade, 05_validate_structural, 06_validate_format, 07_validate_fuzzy, 08_report, 09_approval, 10_finalize, 11_load.

6. Stage 09 is a human gate: the reviewer opens review_package.xlsx and a VBA button or xlwings function writes approved.json or rejected.json into review/{entity}/{RunId}/approval/; a FileSystemWatcher resumes or aborts the run.

7. PDF salvage stage 1: parse.js reads the PDF with pdfjs-dist and writes raw.json (textItems, graphicsOps, canvas size, coordSpace top-left) and raw.stats.json (fonts seen, rect-size histogram, samples).
8. PDF salvage stage 2: render_canvas.py renders the page at 50 DPI by default; slice_canvas.py cuts the PNG into 6 bands by default; the slices are the ground truth for pattern authoring.
9. PDF salvage stage 3: build.js runs clusterLines, classifyLine on every line, groupBlocks, buildDocument, then writes output.docx and output.ir.json; console logs give line-class and block counts.
10. PDF salvage stage 4: preview.js writes preview.html; the author iterates on config.json (labels, regex, thresholds) until the preview matches the slices, then checks the DOCX in Word.

11. Rigor hook (as the skill describes it): Claude Code tests each user prompt against the matcher regex in ~/.claude/settings.json; on a match it runs rigor-reminder.ps1 (timeout 5 s) and injects its output as additional context before the assistant answers.

12. Escalation path (not enabled by default): the reminder writes a marker file, a PreToolUse hook blocks every tool call until the sequential-thinking tool has been invoked, and a Stop hook deletes the marker.

key_functions.name: parse
key_functions.does: Loads the PDF with the pdfjs legacy build, takes page 1 at scale 1.0, maps text items to {id, str, x, y, w, h, fontName, fontSize, color: null, hasEOL} with y flipped to top-left, walks the operator list for path boxes, then writes raw.json and raw.stats.json.
key_functions.expected_output: ./work/raw.json with keys source, canvas {width, height}, coordSpace "top-left", textItems, graphicsOps, images (always []); plus ./work/raw.stats.json

key_functions.name: flushPath
key_functions.does: On a paint operator, transforms each pending path bounding box with the matrix captured when the path was built, flips y, and pushes a graphics op {id, op: "path", x, y, w, h, stroke, fill, opIdx}. Stroke or fill colour is kept only when the paint mode uses it.

key_functions.name: rgb
key_functions.does: Converts pdfjs colour components in the 0..1 range into a lowercase #rrggbb string, clamping each channel; returns null when fewer than three components are given.

key_functions.name: histogramRectSizes
key_functions.does: Buckets graphics ops by their larger side: under 4 tiny, under 16 small, under 100 mid, under 800 large, otherwise huge. Written to raw.stats.json so the author can tell whether real form-field boxes exist.

key_functions.name: clusterLines
key_functions.does: Drops blank items, sorts by y then x, and starts a new line whenever an item is more than yTol points from the y of the item that opened the current line. Each line gets text, xMin, xMax and the mode font size (rounded to 0.1) and mode font name.

key_functions.name: mode
key_functions.does: Most frequent value of an array; a tie keeps the value seen first. Used so one odd glyph does not change a line's font size.

key_functions.name: classifyLine
key_functions.does: Assigns a kind in fixed priority: empty, banner-heading (font size at or above bannerFontSize), form-heading, proc-section (procSection or procQuotite regex), field-label (exact label or label as first item with inline content), temps-total, proc-item (code, desc, optional badge), else body.
key_functions.input_example: one-item line with text "10234 - Description", font 11, formmed5 example config
key_functions.expected_output: { kind: "proc-item", code: "10234", desc: "Description", badge: null, raw: "10234 - Description" }

key_functions.name: groupBlocks
key_functions.does: Folds classified lines into blocks. A form-heading opens a form-question whose rows are label plus content lines (text before the first label becomes preamble); a proc-section opens a proc-list collecting items, notes and a tempsTotal flag. Both stop at the next form-heading, proc-section or banner.

key_functions.name: buildContentParagraphs
key_functions.does: Renders the content cell of a form row. If the label is an option-list host, the joined text starts with optionListPrefix and at least two 'N. text' options are found, it emits a real numbered list with a fresh numbering reference; otherwise one paragraph per line.

key_functions.name: badgeHighlight
key_functions.does: Maps a badge text to a Word highlight colour: exact lowercase key in badgeHighlights first, then any key contained in the badge, else lightGray.
key_functions.input_example: badgeHighlight("30 min") with the formmed5 example config
key_functions.expected_output: "red" (via the "min" key); an unknown badge returns "lightGray"

key_functions.name: NumberingRefs.makeUnique
key_functions.does: Returns a fresh numbering reference and registers a decimal level-0 config for it, so every option list restarts at 1 instead of continuing the previous list.
key_functions.input_example: two calls of makeUnique("opts") on a new instance

key_functions.name: buildDocument
key_functions.does: Dispatches each block kind to its emitter and assembles the docx Document: overridden Heading1 and Heading2 paragraph styles, numbering configs, page margins, a right-aligned italic header with meta.headerText and a 'Page X / Y' footer.

key_functions.name: render
key_functions.signature: def render(pdf_path: str, out_png: str, dpi: int = 50) -> None
key_functions.does: Renders the first page of the PDF with pypdfium2 at scale dpi/72 and saves an optimised PNG, creating the parent directory.

key_functions.name: slice_canvas
key_functions.signature: def slice_canvas(in_png: str, out_dir: str, n: int = 6) -> None
key_functions.does: Cuts a tall PNG into n equal horizontal bands (the last band takes the remainder) named slice-NN-y<top>-<bottom>.png. Pillow's pixel cap is disabled because the canvas is intentionally huge.
key_functions.input_example: a 1200 px tall PNG with the default n

key_functions.name: UserPromptSubmit matcher (rigor regex)
key_functions.does: Decides which prompts get the rigor checklist. Case-insensitive and unanchored; only 'vs' has a word boundary, so the other words also match inside longer words.
key_functions.input_example: "compare option A vs B"  /  "fix the typo in line 3"
key_functions.expected_output: first prompt matches (hook fires); second does not match

infra.detail: Clone the repo and export CLAUDE__ROOT pointing at the clone (bash profile or PowerShell profile). All skill files use ${CLAUDE__ROOT} absolute paths; relative paths are forbidden by the maintenance rules.

infra.topic: Node dependencies of the PDF salvage scripts
infra.detail: scripts/package.json is a private ES-module package: docx ^9.6.1, mammoth ^1.12.0, pdfjs-dist ^5.7.284, optional sharp ^0.34.5. Installed with npm install inside the scripts directory. pdfjs is imported from its legacy build because Node has no DOMMatrix.

infra.topic: Python dependencies of the PDF salvage scripts
infra.detail: pypdfium2 for rendering and Pillow for slicing; installed with pip. No requirements file is committed.

Copy hooks/rigor-reminder.ps1 to ~/.claude/hooks/, merge the UserPromptSubmit entry of references/settings-snippet.json into ~/.claude/settings.json (command type, timeout 5, status message 'Injecting rigor discipline reminder...'), restart Claude Code. Relies on the sequential-thinking MCP server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking) being added at user scope.

Plain GitHub repo, single branch master, no CI, no tests, no build. Updates are manual: copy the changed skill from the source project, commit, push. The deployment skill forbids committing connection strings, API keys, .env files and Bronze CSVs.
Plans produced by write_plan are saved outside the repo at ~/.claude/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md and consumed from there by execute_plan.

decisions.decision: Reference skills locally through ${CLAUDE__ROOT} absolute paths instead of remote plugin or marketplace skills
decisions.why: The owner wants one portable, versioned source of truth that works across machines; if a remote plugin conflicts with a local skill, the local skill takes precedence. Cached plugin paths under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ must not be referenced.
decisions.alternative_rejected: The obra/superpowers plugin, remote marketplace skills, cached plugin paths

decisions.decision: Salvage the working core of a messy pipeline instead of rewriting it
decisions.why: Proven business behaviour must be preserved before style is cleaned; confidence thresholds are deliverables defined before touching code, the clean plan must stay smaller than the legacy workspace, and live writes are refused until boundary and evidence threshold are explicit.
decisions.alternative_rejected: A rewrite, or process metrics such as 'all files migrated' or '100% test coverage' as the definition of done

decisions.decision: New guardrails are wired warn-only first and promoted to hard-block only after a Level 4 staging run
decisions.why: A premature guardrail can block the core path; evidence from a full staging run (for example a false-positive rate under 5%) must justify promotion. If a guardrail blocks too much it is downgraded to probe-only.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Wiring a new gate as a hard block on first integration

decisions.decision: Detect changes with a content hash and a FULL OUTER JOIN between two snapshots instead of CDC
decisions.why: Legacy and commercial source systems give no reliable change feed or updated_at; they only answer 'what is the current state'. Two CSVs and a SQL engine classify every row as NEW, DELETED, MODIFIED or UNCHANGED in one pass, with no hooks or streaming infrastructure.
decisions.alternative_rejected: CDC, event streams, trusting updated_at timestamps

decisions.decision: Numeric-prefixed stage files plus .done sentinels instead of a scheduler or DAG engine
decisions.why: For 10 to 20 stages on one machine an orchestration tool is unjustified overhead. A generic loop sorts filenames and stops on non-zero exit; sentinels give resume-from-failure without an external state store; adding, removing or reordering a stage is a file operation.

decisions.decision: The delta baseline comes from run_registry.json, written only after finalize, never from scanning the filesystem
decisions.why: A failed partial run leaves files with later timestamps than the last good run, so picking the newest file would select a bad baseline. Engine-local load state is kept separately so two engines can upsert into the same staging tables without corrupting each other.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Deriving the previous run from the newest file on disk; one shared state file for all engines

decisions.decision: Rebuild PDF structure from positions and vector operators instead of trusting PDF tags
decisions.why: For forms, templates and scanned documents the structure is visual only (position, font size, proximity); one-shot converters flatten it into paragraphs in scan order. pdfjs-dist exposes both the text stream and the operator list, enough to rebuild structure.
decisions.alternative_rejected: pdf2docx, Acrobat export, mammoth on an already converted file

decisions.decision: Everything corpus-specific lives in config.json; build.js stays corpus-agnostic
decisions.why: The same script must work on a French medical form, an English questionnaire or a contract template. A wrong classification is fixed by adding a label or regex to that corpus's config, not by making the script smarter for one document family.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Hard-coding patterns of one corpus in build.js

decisions.decision: Enforce rigor in the harness with a hook instead of relying on a memory or CLAUDE.md rule
decisions.why: The rule 'use sequential thinking before recommending' already existed in a project feedback memory file and the assistant still skipped it, costing a full review cycle. Memory-only enforcement was judged insufficient, so the harness injects the checklist mechanically.

decisions.decision: Default to the soft UserPromptSubmit reminder (Option 1); keep the blocking PreToolUse hook (Option 2) as an escalation
decisions.why: Option 1 costs nothing per tool call, has cheap false positives and cannot deadlock. Option 2 is hard enforcement but needs three scripts, three settings entries and a marker-file lifecycle, adds about 50 to 200 ms per tool call and can block sequential thinking itself if the allowlist check fails.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Enabling the PreToolUse block from the start

gotchas.issue: The two commands point at ${CLAUDE__ROOT}/dashboard/... and ${CLAUDE__ROOT}/Workflowps/... files that do not exist in this repository.
gotchas.consequence: With CLAUDE__ROOT set to this repo (as the README says) the 'read before writing' step and the Workflowps skill reference cannot be resolved; the commands only work as written inside the icalps-dashboard layout.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Use them from the source project, or repoint the paths (the Workflowps card lives here at skills/workflowps/SKILL.md).

gotchas.issue: The github-deployment skill has drifted from the real repo: it lists writing-plans and executing-plans skills that are absent, recommends a private repo and 'git push origin main', and does not mention the two newer skills.
gotchas.consequence: Following it literally misdescribes the tree; the checkout is on branch master and the orchestrator's inventory lists the repo as public.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Treat the README directory map as the source of truth and refresh the deployment skill.

gotchas.issue: parse.js assigns to an undeclared variable pendingRects in the endPath case; the declared variable is pendingPaths.
gotchas.consequence: By reading (not executed): in an ES module this throws a ReferenceError the first time an endPath operator is handled, and pending paths are never discarded for clip-only paths.

gotchas.issue: Only the first page is processed: parse.js calls getPage(1) and render_canvas.py takes pdf[0], although SKILL.md says single- or multi-page sources are supported.
gotchas.consequence: Pages after the first are silently ignored; the worked example is one very tall canvas page, which hides the limit.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Loop over pages with a per-page y offset before using the skill on a normal multi-page PDF.

gotchas.issue: build.js derives the IR path with outArg.replace(/\.docx$/, ".ir.json").
gotchas.consequence: If the output argument does not end in .docx the IR path equals the output path and the IR JSON overwrites the DOCX just written.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Always pass an output name ending in .docx.

gotchas.issue: Config regexes are case-sensitive unless the pattern starts with the literal prefix (?i); a comment in build.js claims the opposite, and the schema sample in SKILL.md omits the prefix that the real example config uses.
gotchas.consequence: A copied pattern such as '^Section' misses lower-case or upper-case variants and those lines fall through to body.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Prefix patterns with (?i) as the example config does; check line-class counts printed by build.js.

gotchas.issue: Corpus-specific leftovers remain in the 'corpus-agnostic' scripts: preview.js hard-codes the formmed5 title and header, build.js hard-codes the 'Temps total' label and the default 'Options disponibles:' prefix, and usage strings still name old files under src/.
gotchas.consequence: A new corpus gets French labels and the wrong preview title unless the scripts are edited; option texts containing digits also defeat the option-list regex.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Move these literals into config.json when the next corpus is added.

gotchas.issue: Extracted but unused data: graphicsOps are written to raw.json but build.js reads only textItems and canvas; style.colors.badge is loaded and never applied; the optional sharp dependency is never imported; images is always [] and text colour always null.
gotchas.consequence: Rectangles, images and colour play no role in classification yet, despite the description mentioning boxes and visual cues.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Known deferral for colour and images (methodology); rectangle-based field detection is still to be built.

gotchas.issue: The rigor matcher is an unanchored substring regex: tier, design, workflow, approach or production also match inside longer words, and plain mentions of a workflow trigger it.
gotchas.consequence: The checklist is injected on prompts that are not decisions (for example any word containing 'tier').
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Documented stance: narrow the regex locally, or accept the reminder as cheap context noise.

gotchas.issue: The Option 2 blocking script assumes PreToolUse stdin JSON has tool_name and tool_use_history fields; the document itself says this contract is unverified.
gotchas.consequence: If the fields differ, the allowlist check fails and the hook can block the sequential-thinking call itself (deadlock) on rigor-gated turns.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Run the diagnostic variant that logs the received JSON first; rollback is removing the PreToolUse and Stop blocks.

glossary.meaning: Environment variable (two underscores) holding the absolute path of the skills clone; every skill and command path starts with ${CLAUDE__ROOT}.
A command (commands/*.md) is the thing the owner asks Claude to read and follow; a skill (skills/<name>/SKILL.md) is a methodology reference that commands pull in when needed.
The owner's method for recovering the runnable core of a messy, half-understood pipeline without a rewrite.
Three to six measurable behaviours that define 'saved', written before any task; process metrics are not accepted.
File classification of a salvage plan: KEEP, REWRITE-MINIMAL, DEFER, DROP. Every file of the main package goes into exactly one.
One-sentence statement of the gap per system plus at most three file edits per system to close it.
Five ascending risk levels: 1 local contract tests, 2 dry run or server start, 3 read-only live probe, 4 full staging run, 5 approved live write (human approval, no exceptions).
The 12-stage PowerShell Bronze ETL engine of the IC'ALPS project (SQL Server to PostgreSQL stg_ tables). Its code is not in this repo; only its methodology documents are.

Entity contract: name, primary key, updated column, source table, extraction order, staging table, required properties, expected output columns, plus the FK graph. Query contract: the full SQL with JOINs, explicit aliases, ORDER BY primary key and source-side computed fields.
Timestamp identifier (yyyyMMdd_HHmmss) declared once by the orchestrator and threaded to every stage; it namespaces every artifact and sorts chronologically as a string.
Small file {stage_name}_{run_id}.done written by a stage on success; the orchestrator skips stages whose sentinel exists unless -Force is passed.

glossary.term: Run registry vs engine-local load state
glossary.meaning: run_registry.json maps each entity to its last successfully finalized run_id (the delta baseline). Load state files hold engine-internal metadata (row count, schema, fingerprint) per engine.
Risk labels of the Bronze pipeline: BRZ-05 is the 85% schema-coverage threshold (below it, abort before extracting); BRZ-02 flags empty-string foreign keys that silently drop rows in joins.

raw.json is the stage 1 dump of text items and path boxes in top-left coordinates. The IR is the list of classified blocks written next to the DOCX, used to tell a classification error from an emission error.

banner (centred heading with page break), form-question (heading plus two-column label/content table), proc-list (checkbox items with optional badges and a total-time row), field-slot (label plus blank line), paragraph.
Word units used in config.json: table widths and margins are in DXA (1 inch is about 1440), font sizes are in half-points (22 means 11 pt).

Option 1: UserPromptSubmit hook that injects the seven-point discipline checklist (soft). Option 2: PreToolUse hook that blocks tool calls until sequential thinking was invoked, driven by a marker file (hard, deferred).

relations.relation: Its discovery docs survey this repo (scorer_repos.md cites skills/workflowps/INTEGRATIONS.md) and plan to install a new pass-sequence skill into this library following the README conventions (pass_sequence_port.md).

directions: Fix parse.js: rename pendingRects to pendingPaths and loop over all pages, because the skill claims multi-page support but handles page 1 only.
Use graphicsOps in build.js to detect real form-field boxes and checkboxes; rectangles are already extracted and histogrammed but ignored by classification.
Move the remaining formmed5 and French literals (preview title, 'Temps total', option prefix) into config.json and add a second corpus example to prove the corpus-agnostic claim.

If the soft reminder keeps being ignored, verify the PreToolUse JSON contract with the diagnostic logger and then enable Option 2; also tighten the matcher with word boundaries to cut false positives.
coverage_notes: Read all 24 tracked files in full (README, 2 commands, 5 skills with references, 5 scripts, package.json, example config and README, hook script, settings snippet). Nothing was executed: behaviours and expected outputs come from reading simple logic; the parse.js ReferenceError and the pdfjs v5 operator format were not verified by running, so whether stage 1 works end to end with the pinned pdfjs version is uncertain. Shallow clone with one commit (2026-06-10, adds production-discipline), single branch master, no alternate worktrees; 'active' status is a judgement. The Workflowps, dashboard and FastAPI code described by several documents is not in this repo (source project icalps-dashboard is not among the listed projects), so those parts are documentation of external code. The worked-example subdirectory name under skills/salvage-pdf-to-word/examples was deliberately not reproduced because it may be a personal name; a local Windows user path in github-deployment was also left out. Not verified: whether Claude Code applies a matcher to UserPromptSubmit events; if it does not, the reminder fires on every prompt.
